I farm the way I know best: I will keep all 13.1 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, because that fits my land, my water access, and my experience. Since my family has some off-farm work and I am already 68, I will not make the field management too complicated. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put enough fertilizer to hold yield steady, irrigate at the key stages, and keep pest control to the times that matter most. For summer maize, I will switch to a hybrid seed, save labor by using no-tillage after wheat harvest, and rely on both rainfall and my well for water. I will aim for stable production, not take big risks, and keep inputs at a level I can manage confidently on my own land.
